head: A request is a file you can commit.
body: Every request is a .bru file in a plain folder, byte for byte what Bruno writes, so a collection made in Bruno opens here and a diff reads like code. {{variables}} are highlighted, path params get their own table, and the response comes back pretty, raw or as a preview.

head: Bruno's script API, without Node.
body: bru, req, res, test and a chai-style expect run on JavaScriptCore. Chain requests with bru.setVar, jump with setNextRequest, and add declarative asserts — all 29 of Bruno's operators — next to the tests. A script that loops is stopped at 60 seconds instead of wedging the app.

head: Where the 100 ms actually went.
body: DNS, connect, TLS, waiting and download, measured by the system's own task metrics. Below it, the request exactly as it went out, the redirect chain and the cookie jar.

head: Run the whole collection, here or in CI.
body: Sequence order, setNextRequest jumps, tag filters, delay and bail. The same engine runs headless: bidali run . --env staging --reporter junit, from the same binary.

head: Secrets stay out of the repo.
body: Environments are .bru files too, with Bruno's precedence from runtime down to global, .env values as process.env and 35 {{$dynamic}} generators. Secret values live in a 0600 file under your home folder, never in the collection.

head: Every request, one keystroke away.
body: Requests, actions, environments and collections in one palette, with recents first. > for actions, @ for environments, : for collections, and ⌘↩ opens a request and sends it.

head: Paste a curl, get a request.
body: Paste a curl command into the URL bar and it becomes a request with its headers and body. ⌘⇧C copies one back out, resolved or with {{variables}} kept. Postman, OpenAPI, Insomnia, HAR and .http files import too.
